## Introduction

This report demonstrates data visualisation techniques in R using illustrative coral colony measurements. The data are simulated for programming practice and do not represent field observations.

## Prepare the Data

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

coral_df <- data.frame(
  Colony = 1:5,
  Diameter_cm = c(12.5, 15.2, 10.8, 18.4, 14.1),
  Genus = c("Acropora", "Porites", "Acropora",
            "Montipora", "Porites")
)
```

## Scatter Plot

```{r}
ggplot(coral_df, aes(x = Colony, y = Diameter_cm)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Coral Colony Diameters",
    x = "Colony Number",
    y = "Diameter (cm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Histogram

```{r}
ggplot(coral_df, aes(x = Diameter_cm)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 2,
    fill = "lightblue",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Coral Diameters",
    x = "Diameter (cm)",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

## Boxplot

```{r}
ggplot(coral_df, aes(x = "All colonies", y = Diameter_cm)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgreen") +
  labs(
    title = "Coral Diameter Distribution",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Diameter (cm)"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

## Bar Chart

```{r}
ggplot(coral_df, aes(x = Genus)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "lightblue", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Colonies by Coral Genus",
    x = "Coral Genus",
    y = "Number of Colonies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Conclusion

R and ggplot2 provide tools for exploring numerical and categorical marine science data through different graphical representations.
